<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface), recordMcpAccessTokenUse (symbol, a method of class AuthManager; a method of interface IAuthService), verifyMcpAccessToken (symbol, a method of class AuthManager), verifyMcpAccessToken (literal, a string literal in recordMcpAccessTokenUse))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), IAuthService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via resolveExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4663a193741f49b549ab4184841ece0b63bfe1f4` — the merge of head `c67d88b7e97cc357cbdb39d15870cfdbccd59d90` into base `455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4663a193741f49b549ab4184841ece0b63bfe1f4 && git checkout 4663a193741f49b549ab4184841ece0b63bfe1f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 c67d88b7e97cc357cbdb39d15870cfdbccd59d90 && git checkout -B drift-repro 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 && git merge --no-ff c67d88b7e97cc357cbdb39d15870cfdbccd59d90

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e8c0e99184dafa77fc9763791fa4d7fec395dac2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-client-last-use.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/run-after-response.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/core-service-contracts.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx

Inputs read: cards #31211 (body; comments 6710960650, 6711352406, 6712169396) and #30949 (body; comments 6686445086, 6709716960, 6710770858, 6710893443, 6710928373); PR #31247 body, file list and the net diff `origin/main...e8c0e991` (8 files, +332/-57); the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (the two test files, the changeset body as prose, the producer and reader edits as code) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; here it is read, not reviewed.

Gate verdicts on the head at the time of this record: every completed check-run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and all seven Lint lanes, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Plan Test Core shards). Still `in_progress`: Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. None has failed. This record does not wait for them; the queue guard reads them itself.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set.** No Zod schema, no authorable key, no metadata type is touched; `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset. Right.
- **Public surface: one optional member.** `IAuthService` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts`) gains `recordMcpAccessTokenUse?(principal): void`, placed beside `verifyMcpAccessToken`. Its parameter type is derived from the verifier's own declared result (the non-nullable awaited return of `verifyMcpAccessToken`), so the two members cannot drift. Right: the runtime door already aliases the identical derivation as `VerifiedMcpAccessToken` (`resolve-execution-context.ts` line 53), so the door's `authService?.recordMcpAccessTokenUse?.(verifiedTokenPrincipal)` type-checks with no cast.
- **Slot typing.** `ServiceSlotContracts.auth` is `IAuthService` (`core-service-contracts.ts` line 65), so every slot-typed `getService('auth')` reader now sees the member as declared; the door reaches it through that slot, not through `any`, which is what #4127 asked for. Right.
- **api-surface snapshot.** `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` records export names only (`"IAuthService (interface)"`), not members; no new export is added, so no regeneration is owed and none is in the diff. Right. The spec `check:generated` lanes sit in Type Check · workspace, in progress.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` is hand-written prose (not under `content/docs/references/`), updated in the same diff: the member line and a third read-together pair. Right.
- **Producer behaviour change.** `AuthManager.verifyMcpAccessToken` no longer schedules the consent stamp; `AuthManager.recordMcpAccessTokenUse` does. This changes a side effect of a public plugin-auth method, but the side effect has never shipped: the three `.changeset/30918-*` files are still present at the head and every package is at 18.3.0, so no released consumer loses anything. The changeset's host note (call the member once after admitting) is right and sufficient.
- **The declaration.** The `Clause-②:` declaration reads `yes (widening)` on both the PR body and the changeset body, and the diff is a widening: no implementer must add the member, no consumer loses a member or a result field. Right. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right (nothing an author writes changes).

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/31211-mcp-token-use-after-admission.md` declares `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/runtime`. Under this repo's rule (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3) the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`. The kind here is `none`, so `patch` on all three is the level the rule prescribes; generic semver would call an added optional interface member a `minor`, but that is not this repo's rule, and the Check Changeset gate is green on the head. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the changeset body and the PR body, spelled as the rule spells them, and the arm `(widening)` is the one a new optional member takes. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong (three released packages publish). Judged right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions` on the dev report 6712169396:** empty. Nothing to answer.
- **The #30949 open question (report 6710893443, A/B/C):** ruled option A by `domain:server#6` in 6710928373; the diff implements A as the card body of #31211 states it (member in spec, verifier records nothing, WeakMap of returned principals, door call after ban read and after context resolution, pins both ways). Answered by the tree.
- **Deviation 1 (PR footer uses the os-dev session-URL form; model-free commit trailers):** a harness and attribution matter with no bearing on the contract or its code; left to the owning seat, not escalated.
- **Deviation 2 (branch reset from the #30949 base to `origin/main` before the first commit):** nothing had been pushed; the diff is against `origin/main`; no bearing.
- **NOT MEASURED locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exit 3 prerequisite not met):** both need every package's dist; the CI lanes that carry them (Lint · repo & tooling gates: green; Type Check · workspace: in progress) are the gate verdicts. Not a design question; answered by the check-runs.
- **Dev flag: an out-of-tree host that calls `AuthManager.verifyMcpAccessToken` itself no longer gets a stamp.** Answered: the stamp is unreleased (see ①), the repo has exactly one non-test caller of the verifier (the runtime door), and the changeset names the one call such a host adds.
- **Card #30949 serial note (re-read PR #30879's consent read):** #30879 is on `main`; the stamp still picks its consent by `consentForToken` with the verified token's `iat`, now read by `issuedAtOf(token)` inside the verifier's `then`, so the rule is unchanged. Answered.
- **Cross-seat surface:** the plugin-auth and runtime files are named in the spec seat's claim 6711352406 as cross-seat under the triage 6710960650; `domain:server#6` handed the branch over in 6710928373. In bounds.
- **Closing both cards:** the PR body carries `Fixes #31211` and `Fixes #30949`, as triage 6710960650 asked. Right.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts`**, judged against the ruling it implements (option A, record 6710928373), its producer (`AuthManager`) and its reader (the runtime door), and the accepted scenario: a banned subject's verified token stamps nothing; an admitted call stamps exactly once. Each sentence of the new docblock was tried against the live tree at the head.

1. *"Record that the caller ADMITTED a call ... so the provider can keep its coarse last used record of the grant."* True of the producer: `AuthManager.recordMcpAccessTokenUse` (auth-manager.ts line 4673) calls `scheduleMcpClientLastUse`, which runs `McpClientLastUseStamper.record` with the principal plus the token's `iat`; the stamper's consent rule and the one-write-per-consent-per-hour-per-process bound are unchanged from #30918.
2. *"Verifying a token is not admitting the call: the door ... can still refuse it after `verifyMcpAccessToken` answers (a banned subject, an authorization store it could not read)."* True of the reader: `resolve-execution-context.ts` verifies at line 205, then reads the ban at line 211 (`isOAuthSubjectBanned`, outside the verifier's try, so a read fault is `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, 503), then awaits `resolveRequestExecutionContext` (a grant-read fault throws the same class).
3. *"A provider records nothing at verification."* True: the verifier's `then` only sets `verifiedMcpPrincipals` (a WeakMap) and returns the principal; no stamper call remains in `verifyMcpAccessToken`. The producer pin asserts zero reads and zero writes after three verifications.
4. *"The caller calls this member once per admitted call, only after its last refusal has had its say, with the very object `verifyMcpAccessToken` resolved to."* True of the door: the call is at line 305, after the awaited context, and passes `verifiedTokenPrincipal`, which is the verifier's own `verified` object (the spread copy goes to `oauth`, not to the record). The dispatcher calls the door once per request (`http-dispatcher.ts` `timedResolveExecutionContext`, the one call site), so one admitted call is one record. The door pin asserts `toBe(verified)` and length 1. See the should-fix below on how far "its last refusal" reaches.
5. *"A refused call never reaches it, so it is never recorded as a use."* True for every refusal the door makes: a banned subject leaves `verifiedTokenPrincipal` unset; a ban-read fault and a grant-read fault throw before line 305; an unverified token or a verifier that throws leaves it unset; a forward credential never sets it (it is the in-process continuation of a call already recorded). Pinned by the six door cases. I looked for a path where the door returns a guest while `verifiedTokenPrincipal` is set and found none: with `session: { established }` core's `readSession` returns the established user unconditionally (`request-execution-context.ts` line 245), and the ban read is the only row-keyed refusal on this path.
6. *"The provider records only a principal object it returned itself; any other object (a hand-built principal, a copy) records nothing."* True: the WeakMap is keyed by identity; the verifier builds a fresh object literal on every call (`auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`, the `principal: { userId, scopes, ... }` literal in `verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims`), so no two calls share a key and a spread copy misses. Pinned (hand-built and copy record nothing; the control object stamps).
7. *"It returns nothing, never throws and never makes the caller wait."* True: `void`; the whole body is inside `try/catch`; a `null` or primitive argument is guarded before the WeakMap read; the stamp is handed to `runAfterResponse`, which is a `setImmediate` whose task `record` never rejects. Pinned (`null as never` does not throw).
8. *Absence.* The member is optional; the door reaches it with `?.`; an auth service without it admits exactly as before. Pinned (sixth door case). The changeset says the same.
9. *Idempotence.* The contract binds the caller to once per admitted call; the producer is stricter and deletes the WeakMap entry on record, so the same object handed back again (even in a later hour) writes nothing more. Stricter than the text, consistent with it, and pinned. No contradiction.
10. *Other attempted breaks.* Refused calls leave WeakMap entries that die with the principal object: no leak. The `iat` is read from the token the signature just covered, after verification, as before. A door with no data engine answers "not banned" and admits (pre-existing policy of `isOAuthSubjectBanned`); the record follows the door's answer, which is the ruling's whole point. The parameter type's self-reference inside the interface is a deferred indexed-access type TypeScript accepts; Type Check · source gates is green on the head.

**Should-fix (not blocking):** sentence 4 says the member is called "only after its last refusal has had its say"; "its" is the door's, and that is true. But the dispatcher still renders authorization verdicts on the admitted principal after the door has returned and recorded: the environment-membership gate does not skip `/mcp` (`http-dispatcher.ts` `enforceProjectMembership`, skip list `/auth`, `/cloud`, `/health`, `/ready`, `/discovery`), and `domains/mcp.ts` answers `403 insufficient_scope` or `PERMISSION_DENIED` at tool dispatch. Those are verdicts on an identity the door admitted, so recording them as a use of the grant is the right reading and matches the ruling's placement, but the docblock does not say so. One sentence after sentence 4, of the form "an authorization refusal of the admitted principal rendered later (a tool the scopes do not grant, an environment the user is not a member of) is a use and is recorded", would close the gap for the next reader. The mdx pair prose could carry the same clause.

**`content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`** (cited, read): the member line states the same four facts as the docblock (once, after the caller's last refusal, the verifier's object, a foreign object records nothing, never throws, optional) and the new third read-together pair names the door, its two refusals and the authorized-clients reads. The parameter shape is written inline as the verifier's shape, exactly as the `verifyMcpAccessToken` line above it is, so the page is internally consistent. True of the tree.

**Producer and reader (cited, read, not reviewed):** `auth-manager.ts` lines 4616-4735, `mcp-client-last-use.ts` (docblock, `issuedAtOf`, the stamper), `resolve-execution-context.ts` lines 164-172 and 211-214 and 298-306 are what the spec sentences above were judged against; each sentence holds on them. No must-fix found.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review (delta)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `17d06764ef435c656f4c912c77db92ee2b315d9d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts

Delta from the previous record's head `e8c0e991` to this head: one commit, `17d06764e` ("docs(spec): an admitted MCP call refused later for what it asks is still recorded as used"), touching two files, both prose: seven lines added to the `recordMcpAccessTokenUse` docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts` and one sentence appended to the third read-together pair in `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`. The net diff against `origin/main` at this head is the same eight files as before (+339/-57 versus +332/-57); no code, test or changeset line moved. The previous record's ①, ②, ③ and ④ items 1-3 and 5-10 stand unchanged on this head.

Gate verdicts on this head at the time of this record: completed and `success`: Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards; `skipped`: the opt-in harnesses and the schedule gate; everything else (Check Changeset, the seven Lint lanes, Spec property liveness, the four Type Check lanes, Flag docs, filter, and the Build and Test lanes they fan out to) is `in_progress`. None has failed. This record does not wait for them; the queue guard reads them itself.

### The should-fix from the previous record

Asked for: one sentence bounding "only after its last refusal has had its say" so that an authorization verdict rendered on the admitted principal later in the request is named as a use that is recorded.

Delivered, in the docblock: "Admitting is the decision about WHO calls, not every later authorization verdict: once the principal is admitted, a refusal of what it then asks for, rendered further down the request (the MCP domain's 403 `insufficient_scope` for a token that grants none of the MCP tool families, a tool the token's scopes leave unregistered, an action whose scope family the token was not granted), is still a use of the grant, and it is recorded." The mdx pair carries the same clause in shorter form.

Each clause tried against the live tree at this head:

- *"the MCP domain's 403 `insufficient_scope` for a token that grants none of the MCP tool families"* — true: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` lines 130-146 answer 403 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"` when `ec.oauthScopes` names none of `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES`; `ec` is the context the door returned, so the record at `resolve-execution-context.ts` line 305 has already run.
- *"a tool the token's scopes leave unregistered"* — true: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` line 222 (`grantedScopes`) narrows registration to the granted families, fail-closed, an empty array registering nothing; the dev's report spelled this as a runtime path at about line 2220, but the mechanism is the one named and it is in `packages/mcp` at line 222. The record precedes it.
- *"an action whose scope family the token was not granted"* — true: `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` `apiForwardScopeFamilyRefusal` (line 1845; called at line 1759 for an agent carried by a forward credential) answers 403 with the scope the agent lacks. The forward credential is the continuation of an already recorded call (previous record, ④ item 5), so this refusal follows the record too.
- *"Admitting is the decision about WHO calls"* — true of the door: every refusal the door makes (ban, ban-read fault, grant-read fault, unverified token) decides whether the token resolves to a principal and runs before line 305; nothing after that line changes who the principal is.
- *The environment-membership gate, deliberately not named* — right not to name it for a bearer-only call: `http-dispatcher.ts` `enforceProjectMembership` (lines 1589-1702) reads the caller only through `api.getSession(inProcessSessionReadInput(headers))`, the auth service's session read; a request carrying only an MCP JWT bearer resolves no session there, `userId` stays unset, and the gate returns `null` at "Anonymous requests — upstream auth will decide" (line 1705). So it never refuses a bearer-only agent. The one way it could refuse after the record is a session cookie riding beside the bearer whose user is not a member; that is a refusal of the cookie's user, and it falls under the sentence's general clause ("a refusal ... rendered further down the request ... is still a use of the grant, and it is recorded") without needing to be named. The ADR-0069 `enforceAuthGate` has the same shape (session read; no cookie, no gate) and the same answer.
- *Attempts to break the sentence:* I looked for a verdict rendered after line 305 that would make the principal not the token's user or would un-admit it, and found none; the dispatcher's later gates either exit as nobody for a bearer-only call or refuse what the principal asks for. I looked for a refusal of "what it asks for" rendered before the record, which would make "is recorded" false; the MCP domain, the MCP runtime and the action door all run on the returned context, so none precedes it. The list in parentheses is illustrative and introduced as examples, so an unnamed later verdict (a `PERMISSION_DENIED` from a tool's own permission check, a walled-catalog write refusal) is covered by the general clause and does not falsify it.

The should-fix is closed. The sentence is true of the producer, the reader and every later refusal on the MCP path at this head, and the mdx says the same thing in the same terms.

### New findings

None must-fix. None should-fix. The only inexactness found is in the dev's report, not in the tree: the narrowing lives at `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` line 222, not in a runtime file at about line 2220; the docblock itself names no path, so nothing in the published text is wrong.

## Contract review (delta)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c67d88b7e97cc357cbdb39d15870cfdbccd59d90`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-client-last-use.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts

Second delta, after the records on `e8c0e991` and `17d06764`. The head moved by one commit, `c67d88b7`, "Merge branch 'main' into claude/project-thread-p0qal7", a base update the seat ran because Test UI shard 5/16 was cancelled at its timeout on `17d06764`.

### The merge is pure
